preview: Sahil Kedare shares his 4-round interview experience at Wells Fargo for the Program Associate role, featuring an AMCAT online test, two technical/managerial rounds, and an HR round resulting in a full-time offer.
content: Wells Fargo Interview Experience Sahil Kedare | Final Year BTech Computer Engineering 2019-23 Wells Fargo visited our campus in August 2022 to hire ﬁnal year students for the role of Program Associate. Branches allowed were: Computer Engineering , Information Technology, Electronics & Telecommunication, Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering. They mentioned the minimum pointer should be 6.5. But further shortlisting was done and only the students with pointer >=8 received the test link. Whole process was conducted virtually. Total 4 rounds were conducted overall. 1. Online test 2. Technical Round 1 3. Technical + Managerial Round 4. HR Round Round 1: Online Test (1hr 40 minutes) This was an AMCAT test hosted on SHL platform (Aspiring Minds platform). There was no negative marking, and we cannot move backwards once a question is submitted (Except the coding section). There were 3 sections: 1. Verbal Ability (12 MCQs in 15 mins): Had standard English questions asked in any AMCAT test like correct the sentence, ﬁll up with the appropriate word, synonyms, arrange the jumbled parts of a sentence and a passage at the end . 2. Business Aptitude (15 MCQs in 25mins): Had several case studies.The questions were to test how well you analyze and understand the given data. Speed was key here and for each question two questions were there one after another and 2 graphs/tables so don't waste time analyzing all the data, read the question and accordingly look for the relevant table/graph. 3. Coding (2 questions in 60mins): a. An online shopping website provides home delivery for products ordered online. N delivery persons are assigned to deliver parcels in the city. Customers may update the delivery address located, even after the delivery is scheduled. If the delivery location is updated, the delivery person is informed of the extra distance in a message separately. If the new location is outside the range, he receives extra compensation. As per the rules, this kind of compensation is only given once. There are 2 types of queries ● Print the sum of the salaries of the required delivery persons. ● Update the salary with the extra compensation for the employee. Input : First line contains 3 integers : number of delivery men, range, extra compensation. Next it contains q: number of queries. Type 1 Query: queryType, start id, end id Type 2 Query : queryType, delivery men id, distance. b. Given n athletes participating in a relay race with some details of how the batons should be passed on. We had to find a way to pass the batons such that the cost(distance) is minimum. (I dont remember the exact question. This question had to be solved using topological sort) Input : First line contains n: number of athletes. Next it contains m: number of baton passes. Each of the mth line has two integers denoting the id of athletes from which the baton is to be passed eg. (1-2) baton is passed from athlete 1 to athlete 2. I solved most of the questions from the verbal ability and business aptitude section. In the coding part, I solved the 1st question and passed 10/13 test cases. In the second question, I applied some brute force logic and cleared only 2 or 3 test cases. The verbal and aptitude sections are equally important to clear this round. 22 students cleared this round. Round 2: Technical Interview (35 minutes) This round was scheduled at 9 am in the morning. Interviewer was very friendly and he introduced himself and then asked me to introduce myself. He asked questions from DBMS. ● What is a DBMS? ● What is Normalization? ● SQL and NoSQL databases. Then he gave me 2 bank scenario one of them was : ● Consider that Wells Fargo has a loan program where each region has a specific loan limit. for ex. People residing in region xyz can apply for a loan of 1 lakh without any details or proper verification etc. So I had to find a solution on how I could help Wells to handle this. We had a detailed discussion on this. Further he asked me to describe a project of mine in detail and asked many questions about it. Some of them were : ● What was my role? ● What challenges did I face? ● Why did I choose this particular tech stack? ● What was the best or most appreciated feature in this project? In my resume I had mentioned that I won the code for good (CFG) hackathon by JPMC so he thought that I already had an offer from JPMC but I did not have. Then we discussed my hackathon experience. I had done a summer internship at an ed-tech based startup GroundUp so the interviewer asked me about my experience working there, what work I did and what were the learnings etc Finally while looking through my resume he saw that in my hobbies I had mentioned movies so he was very happy and told me that he also watches movies a lot.We had a good discussion on movies and he asked me what movies genres i liked and why, and a movie that I can't forget ever. Then the interviewer asked me if I had any questions for him (always ask), I asked a few questions and the interview ended. I was not asked a single dsa question while some of my friends were asked (Depends on the interviewer).14 people were selected for round 3. Round 3: Technical + Managerial Interview (25 minutes) As soon as my round 2 got over I was informed that I am selected for round 3 scheduled at 10.30 am. The interviewer was not very friendly compared to the previous interviewer and did not switch on her camera, she directly asked me to introduce myself. After that she asked me to explain my recent project in detail. Why did I use this particular tech stack, its advantages etc. We had a detailed discussion on my project. She then asked me till now you have worked on modern technologies/languages so how will you manage if you have to work on older technologies. She asked me if I had any questions for her. I asked a few questions and the interview ended. (Actually more questions were asked but I remember only these😅). 8 people were shortlisted for the HR round. Round 4: (HR Round) This round happened after a long time after the 3rd round at 4pm. It was a telephonic round. HR asked me a few basic questions like: how was your day, are you willing to relocate. She then asked if I was clear with the compensation details and the breakup.Then she asked if I had any questions for her and the interview ended. The results were announced at around 5pm in the evening, and a total of 8 students were selected for a full time oﬀer and I was one of them. Some Tips to ace your interview: For DSA & CS Fundamentals : ● Practice problems from 450dsa.com, GeeksForGeeks and Leetcode. ● Do refer to this, it has all the resources for preparation. ● Make sure you prepare CS Fundamentals along with DSA. Study them thoroughly. ● Refer this doc, it will answer most of your questions regarding preparations and resources.Be prepared with all the concepts from each of them very clearly. For Interviews: ● The most important thing is to stay calm and be confident. A lot depends on your confidence. ● Join the interview link at least 5 minutes prior to the time allotted to you. It gives an impression that you are punctual. ● Dont Lie in your resume or don't mention anything which you would not be able to answer. Always be honest. ● Prepare your introduction by heart, don't leave it for the end. ● Practice HR questions and research well about the company. ● Always ask questions at the end of the interview. It shows your interest in their company. ● Always read interview experiences from gfg before your interviews/test. They give you a fair idea of what type of questions are asked in a particular company and also you feel a little prepared. All the best !!
